en: Vimānavatthu: The Chapter on the Woman’s Mansion,
Section on the Seats (Pīṭhavagga)
8. The Third Mansion of the Ship “O woman,
you stand having boarded a ship with a golden canopy.”
You plunge into the lotus pond and pluck the lotus with your hand;
your dwellings are gabled mansions.
Divided and measured out into portions,
they shine brilliantly,
radiating light in all four directions.
By what means is your complexion so radiant?
By what means do you prosper here?
And by what means do your riches arise?
"Whatever is dear to the mind—
O goddess of great majesty, I ask you:
what merit did you perform when you were a human being?"
“By whom have you been made thus radiant in power,
that your complexion shines forth in all directions?
The deity, delighted, [replied:]
Questioned by the Fully Awakened One himself,
she answered the question that was asked,
the fruit of which action this is.
“In a former birth, while among humans in the human world,
having seen monks who were thirsty and weary, I— ”
Having risen, I gave water for them to drink.
Indeed, whoever rises and gives water to those who are weary and thirsty;
There are rivers for him with cool waters,
abundant with flowers and many white lotuses;
streams flow around it at all times.
The river with its cool waters and sand-banks;
the mango, sal, tilaka, and rose-apple trees;
and the blooming uddālaka and pāṭali flowers.
That supreme mansion, endowed with various grounds and shining intensely,
is the ripening of this very karma here.
Those who have performed such merit obtain this:
"My gabled houses are well-constructed,
divided into sections and measured out."
Shining brightly, they illuminate the four directions all around. Because of that,
my complexion is such as this.
By that, I succeed here;
and whatever riches arise for me that are dear to the mind, they come to pass.
I declare to you, O Buddha of great majesty:
when I was a human being, I performed meritorious deeds;
it is because of that that I am thus ablaze with power.
"And my complexion shines in all directions;
this is the fruit of that deed,
that for my benefit the Buddha drank the water."
The third Ship Mansion; the eighth [chapter].
